::: {.notes}
`visibility="uncounted"` is what keeps these out of the slide count and off the
progress bar. Put it on every appendix slide.

⚠️ LEARN THE NUMBERS FOR THREE OR FOUR OF THESE AND WRITE THEM ON A CARD.
Hunting through the `m` menu while a senior person waits costs you more than the
slide gains you. Typing a number and pressing Enter is instant.
:::

## What an appendix slide is for {#apx-purpose visibility="uncounted"}

::: {.keylines}
::: {.lead}
**It answers a question out loud**

One slide, one question, and the title IS the answer. Not a dump of what did not
fit in the talk.
:::
::: {}
**Build it from the questions you expect**

List what a hostile listener will ask. Every item needing a picture, a table or
a number becomes one appendix slide.
:::
::: {}
**A slide you cannot find is a slide you do not have**

Know the number. Searching while someone waits costs more than the slide gains.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
The discipline here is the same as for the main deck. An appendix slide whose
title is "Robustness checks" makes the room read the whole slide to find out
whether it answers them. "The result holds when the outliers are dropped" does
not.
:::

## Numbers that are not final yet {#apx-provisional .provisional visibility="uncounted"}

::: {.statement}
A number on a projected slide is read by the room and written down. A number in
a draft is not.
:::

::: {.notes}
This slide carries the `.provisional` class, which draws a faint corner tag.
Look at the top right.

It is legible to you in speaker view and effectively invisible from the back of
a room at 1/6 opacity. The point is that you cannot forget which slides are
carrying unfinished numbers, because grepping the sources for "provisional" is
the whole checklist.

Delete the class as each analysis settles.
:::
